checkpoint.declared_transformers_version_note: older than the version the model card tells you to install (4.57.1); the card wins, and the preflight is what proves the remote code still resolves under it

framework_floor_audit.required: model card: torch==2.10.0, torchvision==0.25.0, transformers==4.57.1, plus Pillow==12.1.1, matplotlib==3.10.8, einops==0.8.2, addict==2.4.0, easydict==1.13, pymupdf==1.27.2.2, psutil==7.2.2; tested on python 3.12.3 + CUDA 12.9. model_type unlimited-ocr is not transformers-native; it loads from auto_map.
framework_floor_audit.image_ships: nvidia/cuda:12.9.1-cudnn-runtime-ubuntu24.04 - no python and no ML stack at all (D18), so bootstrap.sh builds a venv and installs every card pin itself
framework_floor_audit.action: no pin change - bootstrap.sh already installs the card's exact list. It gains an architecture preflight that resolves the checkpoint through AutoConfig(trust_remote_code=True) under the pinned transformers, which is the one thing the version numbers alone cannot tell you.

cuda_floor.source: base image CUDA runtime, matched by the torch wheel this runtime installs
cuda_floor.vendor_documented_floor: none published: the vendor documents no driver floor beyond the image's own CUDA runtime
cuda_floor.rationale: min_cuda_version is the lowest CUDA version a RunPod host may report for this runtime to start. It is sent as the create payload's allowedCudaVersions -- every version RunPod lists at or above it -- because pod 3xag0y00rgoj4n ran this campaign's CUDA 12.9 image on a host reporting cudaVersion 12.8 and died in torch._C._cuda_init with CUDA error 804 after the pod was already billing. Read anonymously from the pinned image's own OCI config blob at the digest runtime.json pins; nothing is inferred from the image name.
